data.title: Kraken Parent Payward Wins In-Principle Approval For Kazakhstan Expansion
data.description:
TL;DR: Payward has received in-principle approval for a Kazakhstan business covering digital asset trading, dealing and custody in the AIFC. Final licensing conditions remain relevant, and the announcement gives no customer launch date.

Kraken parent Payward has moved closer to establishing a regulated business in Kazakhstan, with preliminary approval for several activities rather than trading alone.

In an October 22 announcement, Payward said the Astana Financial Services Authority had granted in-principle approval to license Payward Kazakhstan in the Astana International Financial Centre. The proposed permissions cover operating a digital asset trading facility, dealing in investments as principal and agent, and digital asset custody.

The company also said Kazakh traders would gain access to its global order books. It did not give a date for the local service to open. For prospective local customers, the distinction between that plan and a completed launch is the most immediate detail.

The License Still Has A Final Stage

AFSA’s authorization guide explains that in-principle approval sets out conditions and recommendations an applicant must satisfy before receiving its license. The process can involve establishing a legal entity, injecting capital and resolving other regulatory matters.

The guide also says applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial and human resources, systems and internal controls for the activities they propose. Those are general licensing requirements; Payward’s brief announcement does not disclose the particular conditions attached to its own approval.

That makes the announcement evidence of progress through the licensing process. It is not evidence that every planned product is already available or that the same permissions apply outside the AIFC. Customers ultimately need to know which local entity provides a service and exactly what that entity is licensed to do.

Local Permissions, A Global Order Book

The proposed combination is commercially significant because an exchange serves more than one function. Trading brings buyers and sellers together; dealing permissions concern how the firm participates in transactions; custody concerns responsibility for customers’ assets.

Those functions can sit behind a single app, but their risks differ. A competitive execution price says little about the handling of a withdrawal dispute, just as a strong custody arrangement does not guarantee a deep trading market.

Access to wider order books could be useful if the eventual service connects local demand with more counterparties. That potential benefit should be assessed through actual execution quality, fees and withdrawal arrangements once services are available. The announcement alone cannot establish those outcomes.

For traders considering Bitcoin or other digital assets through the planned operation, the next concrete milestone is the final license and a clear description of the products, eligible customers and opening date. The preliminary approval advances that process while leaving those practical questions to the next stage.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: High dividend, low price: 4 stocks under Rs.200 with high yield - IOCL, PTC India, Central Bank, PTL Enterprises
data.description:

The metric helps investors to identify stocks with attractive dividend yields and help them earn decent annual dividend income relative to the money they invest.

PTL Enterprises has announced Rs.2.5 per share dividend over the last one year. Its annual yield stood at 6.25% for the year 2026.

Annual dividend yield is the percentage of the amount used to purchase a stock and the dividend income earned from it over the period of one year. IT matters because it helps investors to understand the cash return they get per Rupees invested in a stock.

data.title: Infosys headcount rises by 4,480 in Q2FY27, freshers hiring crosses 8,000; check details
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Infosys, India's second-largest IT services company, reported a net addition of 4,480 employees in the second quarter of FY27. The company's total workforce stood at 332,542 at the end of the July-September period. This marked a clear recovery after a decline of 532 employees in the previous quarter. The net addition for the first half of FY27 now stands at 3,948 employees.

The Bengaluru-based firm onboarded more than 8,000 college graduates during the September quarter. This is double the number of freshers it hired in the preceding three months. Infosys has reiterated its full-year target of recruiting around 20,000 fresh graduates.

Speaking at the company's Q2 earnings conference, Salil Parekh, CEO and MD, Infosys said, "We hired 8,000 college graduates in Q2. Our full-year target remains 20,000. We have done more than half of that in H1FY27."

The continued focus on campus hiring signals that the company is preparing for demand in areas such as artificial intelligence and large-scale digital transformation projects, even as overall industry growth remains measured.

Voluntary attrition at Infosys moderated to 12.7 percent on a last-twelve-month basis, down from 13 percent in the previous quarter. The improvement suggests better employee retention as the industry navigates a phase of selective hiring and skill-specific demand.

Peer performance varied widely in the same quarter. Tata Consultancy Services added 4,258 employees. HCLTech recorded the highest net addition among large peers at 6,450. Tech Mahindra's headcount rose by 5,446. In contrast, Wipro saw a sequential decline of 6,716 employees. These mixed trends highlight that while some firms are expanding their base to capture emerging opportunities, others are prioritising efficiency and cost management.

Infosys announced its second-quarter results on October 23. Net profit rose 6 percent to Rs.7,823 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared with Rs.7,364 crore in the year-ago period. Growth was supported by stronger demand from energy and utilities clients and higher spending on artificial intelligence services.

Revenue from operations increased 11 percent to Rs.49,244 crore from Rs.44,490 crore in Q2FY26. Large deal total contract value for the quarter reached $5.2 billion, up from $3.6 billion in the previous quarter.

However, the company revised its revenue growth guidance for FY2026-27 to 1-2 percent in constant currency terms, down from the earlier range of 1.5-3 percent. It maintained its operating margin guidance at 20-22 percent. The guidance cut reflects cautious client spending in certain verticals even as deal wins and AI-related work provide pockets of strength.

The combination of net headcount addition, sustained fresher intake, and moderating attrition points to a stabilising workforce strategy at Infosys. While the lowered growth outlook indicates that the broader demand environment remains uneven, the company's hiring momentum and strong large-deal performance suggest it is positioning itself for selective growth opportunities in the second half of the year.

data.title: Reliance Jio IPO: Who is Arjun Vaidya? Bizman shares why his friend Akash Ambani returned to India from US | Video
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Reliance Jio's record-breaking initial public offering (IPO) has prompted entrepreneur and investor Arjun Vaidya to recall a conversation from 2013, when his friend Akash Ambani decided to return to India after graduating from Brown University in the US to pursue what he described as an ambitious vision of building Jio.

In a video shared on Instagram, Vaidya recounted how Akash had spoken about bringing affordable, high-speed internet to Indians at a time when the idea appeared far-fetched. 13 years later, he said, that vision had culminated in India's biggest-ever IPO, attracting unprecedented investor interest.

Jio Platforms' Rs.30,213-crore public issue closed on October 23 with subscriptions of 22.19 times the shares on offer. Total demand, including the anchor investor placement, crossed Rs.7.4 lakh crore, while the number of applications approached 1.39 crore, according to stock exchange data.

Reflecting on his friend's journey, Vaidya said, "In 2013, Akash and I graduated from Brown and he left with the wildest dream I'd ever heard. Yesterday, that dream became India's biggest IPO ever."

Vaidya said that while many of their classmates chose to remain in the US and pursue careers in cities such as New York and San Francisco, Akash was among those who decided to return to India.

"When we graduated from Brown in 2013, almost all of our friends were staying back in the US, taking jobs in New York, San Francisco. But Akash was one of the few of us packing his bags and coming home, because his dad had given him a dream, which was to build Jio," he recalled.

According to Vaidya, Akash would frequently discuss his ambition of making 4G connectivity and high-speed internet accessible to people across India.

"He would sit with us and talk about 4G and data in every Indian's pocket, internet speed as fast as we had in college in the US," Vaidya said, adding that the idea seemed almost unbelievable in 2013 and 2014.

He also recalled watching the 2013 IPL final on an early prototype of what eventually became the JioTV app. The possibility of watching live cricket on a mobile phone had seemed extraordinary at the time, he said.

Arjun Vaidya, 35, is an Indian entrepreneur, venture capitalist and angel investor, best known for founding the direct-to-consumer (D2C) Ayurvedic wellness brand Dr. Vaidya's and co-founding V3 Ventures.

A graduate of Brown University, Vaidya completed his studies in 2013 before beginning his career in private equity with L Catterton, an investment firm focused on consumer businesses. He subsequently moved into entrepreneurship, drawing on his family's legacy in Ayurveda to establish Dr. Vaidya's in 2016.

Under his leadership, the company grew into a prominent online Ayurvedic brand, reaching more than two million customers and expanding its portfolio to over 80 products. In 2021, the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group acquired a majority stake in the business.

Vaidya later co-founded V3 Ventures, backed by Belgian investment group Verlinvest, to invest in early-stage consumer businesses. He is also an active angel investor and mentor to startups in India's consumer ecosystem.

Vaidya credited Jio's expansion with changing the way Indians access the internet and creating opportunities for businesses across sectors.

"Today, every single Indian just takes that for granted," he said, referring to the widespread availability of mobile internet.

He added that his own entrepreneurial journey and the businesses he had founded or invested in were closely connected to the digital ecosystem enabled by affordable data.

"The entire startup ecosystem, I would say, is a byproduct of the world Jio created," Vaidya said.

He also pointed to the growth of digital payments and direct-to-consumer businesses, noting that UPI processes 24 billion transactions a month and that consumers increasingly discover and purchase products through their phones.

Discussing the IPO's response, Vaidya highlighted that the qualified institutional buyers (QIB) portion was fully subscribed in less than 100 minutes. He described the strong participation as evidence of how widely Indians identify with Jio's growth story.

He also recalled Akash calling him late on the night the IPO opened to discuss what the development meant for the D2C industry and what lessons other businesses could draw from it.

Vaidya said his friend expressed hope that future IPOs would receive a similarly strong response from institutional investors on their opening day.

Concluding his video, Vaidya reflected on how returning to India, which appeared to be the riskier choice for graduates in 2013, has become an increasingly attractive option.

"13 years ago, coming back to India was the risky choice. Now everyone seems to be doing it," he said.

data.title: Less EMI tip: Can you switch your home loan lenders multiple times? What it costs to do so, when you should consider it?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- A home loan balance transfer facility allows borrowers to move their loan to another lender before the loan tenure ends, usually to secure a lower interest rate. The new lender evaluates the application as a fresh loan and if approved, repays the outstanding amount to the existing lender.

Once the transfer process is done, you begin repaying the remaining loan amount to the new lender at the revised interest rate.

However, a balance transfer is not necessarily a one-time option. Borrowers may consider switching lenders again if another lender offers a more competitive interest rate or more favourable terms.

Yes, there is no fixed legal limit on the number of times you can transfer a home loan. Borrowers can switch lenders multiple times, provided they meet the new lender's eligibility criteria and the loan is approved by the new lender.

As mentioned earlier, most borrowers shift their loans to another lender when they are being offered lower interest rates.

For example, if you got a home loan of Rs.25 lakh at a 7% interest rate for 20 years. The approximate total interest due for payment will be Rs.21.5 lakh. However, if another lender offers a reduced interest rate of 6%, your total interest amount would be almost Rs.18 lakh, saving an amount of Rs.3.5 lakh.

Apart from a lower interest rate, refinancing your home loan can offer other benefits, such as restructuring the repayment tenure to arrive at a more manageable EMI. Some lenders may also offer additional facilities, including top-up loans, doorstep services and better customer support.

However, transferring your home loan multiple times may not always be financially beneficial. According to a blog post by Kotak Mahindra Bank, borrowers should consider the following factors first:

If you have a fixed rate home loan, the current lender can impose prepayment charges of up to 2% of the outstanding loan amount, according to a blog post by ICICI Bank. The levy varies between lenders.

Also, transferring a home loan is similar to taking a new home loan from a new lender. The new lender will also charge a processing fee on the loan amount.

If your home loan is under the floating rate regime, then your current bank cannot levy any prepayment charges as per directions from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). However, in this case too, the new lender may charge you a processing fee for the loan being transferred to another lender.

data.title: Kotak Bank sees margins stabilizing as FCNR drag offsets repo gains
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 24 -- Kotak Mahindra Bank expects its net interest margin (NIM) to remain around the second-quarter level in the coming quarters as the full impact of high-cost foreign currency non-resident bank or FCNR(B) deposits is offset by the repricing of repo-linked loans and the deployment of surplus funds into higher-yielding customer assets, outgoing managing director and chief executive office Ashok Vaswani said.

"We will see margins in the same region as Q2," Vaswani said while answering a question during the bank's September-quarter earnings call on Saturday. He said the impact of FCNR(B) deposits would continue into the third and fourth quarters of FY27.

For the quarter ended September, the bank's NIM fell to 4.31% from 4.53% in the previous quarter and 4.54% a year earlier.

FCNR(B) deposits and advances against them contributed about 15 basis points to the sequential decline of 22 basis points, while day-count variation and the repayment of inter-bank participation certificate (IBPC) borrowings accounted for the remainder, chief financial officer Devang Gheewalla said.

As part of a wider push to attract dollars into India and prop up a sagging rupee, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on 5 June had announced subsidized windows to tap overseas debt. While the FCNR(B) deposit scheme ended preemptively on 31 August, those for external commercial borrowings (ECB) and overseas foreign currency borrowings remain open till 31 December.

Till 18 September, these windows had led to inflows of $143.6 billion, with 93% coming through FCNR deposits, RBI data showed.

Kotak Bank mobilized around Rs.55,344 crore through FCNR(B) deposits. Of this, Rs.16,110 crore was deployed as advances against the deposits, while part of the funds was used to finance the loan portfolio transferred from Kotak Mahindra Investments Ltd and replace relatively expensive IBPC borrowings. The remaining liquidity will be deployed over the next few quarters, Gheewalla said.

About 60% of the bank's advances are repo-linked, allowing higher interest rates to feed through as loans are repriced. Management said the full impact of repo transmission should be reflected in margins in Q4, while deploying FCNR funds would take a few quarters.

Total deposits grew 23% year-on-year to Rs.6.51 trillion, or 13% excluding FCNR(B) deposits. Average deposits increased 19% to Rs.6.06 trillion. Net advances grew 25% to Rs.5.77 trillion, or 19% excluding advances against FCNR(B) deposits and the acquired loan portfolio.

Customer assets, including credit substitutes, stood at Rs.6.27 trillion, up 23% year-on-year. The CASA ratio declined to 38.2% from 42.3% a year earlier, while the cost of funds improved to 4.52% from 4.70%.

Net interest income (NII) rose 16% year-on-year to Rs.8,459 crore in Q2, while net profit increased 29% to Rs.4,212 crore

Gross non-performing assets ratio of the bank fell to 1.04% from 1.18% a quarter ago and 1.39% a year earlier, while net NPA ratio declined to 0.24% from 0.27% a quarter and 0.32% a year ago.

Management said it was not seeing broad-based stress across its portfolios but remained watchful amid difficult conditions. In tractor financing, it flagged a 13% rainfall deficit as a concern in some regions, while saying the portfolio was performing well and there was no immediate impact.

"We do watch the weather condition," management said, adding that the bank would remain vigilant as conditions evolved. Collection efficiency in the small commercial vehicle portfolio was also improving month-on-month.

Festive demand remained steady overall, though the bank said it would monitor regional variations and rural conditions closely.

data.title: IDBI Bank sale: Employees' service conditions to remain unchanged, says DIPAM Secretary
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Service conditions of IDBI Bank employees will remain unchanged after the proposed sale of the lender to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings, a senior government official said on Friday, seeking to allay concerns among staff and pensioners over the strategic disinvestment.

Arunish Chawla, Secretary of the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM), said existing employees and pensioners had "nothing to fear" from the proposed sale of more than 60% of the bank's equity for Rs.52,878 crore.

"As per the share purchase agreement, the service conditions of the existing employees cannot be changed, modified or altered to their disadvantage by the strategic buyer," Chawla told PTI.

His remarks come amid protests by IDBI Bank employees against the government's disinvestment plan. Bank staff have called for a strike across branches in early November, with the United Forum of Bank Unions also extending support to the proposed agitation.

Addressing concerns over retirement benefits, Chawla said a dedicated pension fund had been set aside and all commitments to pensioners would continue to be honoured.

He also clarified that IDBI Bank is not a nationalised bank and that its employees' service conditions are determined by the bank's board in consultation with employees, rather than directly by the government.

"IDBI Bank is being restructured as a going concern and even in future it will be a board-managed company. It works under the company and labour law today; it will continue to work under the company and labour law tomorrow," Chawla said.

The government and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) intend to remain public shareholders in IDBI Bank after the strategic sale, with their respective equity holdings capped at 15% and without representation on the bank's board, Chawla said earlier in the week.

Following the restructuring, responsibility for managing the bank and providing additional capital whenever required would rest with the strategic buyer, he told PTI.

"Both the Government of India and LIC want to become public shareholders. To become public shareholders, you cannot hold more than 15 per cent equity. You also cannot sit on the board. Otherwise, you have the same contingent liability for the bank as a promoter has," he said.

The market regulator has also directed LIC to reduce its stake in IDBI Bank from 19% on a post-diluted basis to 15%. The reduction would increase the bank's public float by four percentage points, making additional shares available to retail investors and other public shareholders.

Last week, the government approved the sale of a combined 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for approximately Rs.53,000 crore, or $5.5 billion.

The transaction comprises the government's 30.48% holding, valued at around Rs.26,620 crore, and LIC's 30.24% stake, worth approximately Rs.26,440 crore.

Fairfax, led by Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa, has offered Rs.81 per share, exceeding the benchmark fair value of Rs.75.99 determined by two independent valuation agencies.

The proposed transaction would represent the largest foreign investment in an Indian bank and mark a significant step in India's long-delayed banking privatisation programme.

The strategic sale is expected to be completed by the end of the current financial year, subject to regulatory approvals, including clearance from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

Once the transaction is completed, Fairfax will assume responsibility for running the bank and meeting its future capital requirements.

The proposed ownership change has triggered opposition from employees concerned about their service conditions and retirement benefits. The government's assurances on employment terms and pension commitments come as the bank prepares for a possible nationwide strike in early November.

data.title: How Trade Desk Rescued Executives' Stock Options From a Dive in the Share Price — WSJ
data.description:
By Theo Francis

Trade Desk shareholders have contended with a 66% slump in the stock price so far this year. This week, Chief Executive Jeff Green gave himself — and many of his employees — a do-over.

The advertising technology company repriced 1.6 million options for Green, another 1.6 million for other senior executives, plus millions more spread across more than 2,000 other employees. The move transformed the options from deeply underwater to slightly in the money as of Friday, when Trade Desk closed at $13 a share.

In a securities filing, the company said it had been concerned the share price's tumble could "substantially harm" its ability to retain employees who hold the options.

Corporate executives often get much of their pay in the form of stock or options, as a way to motivate and reward them for the stock's appreciation. In turn, if the stock slumps, they receive less — or from options, potentially nothing. When Trade Desk slashed the cost to exercise options by as much as 85%, to $12.26, it effectively wiped away months of losses other investors have borne.

Repricing is rare and often opposed by investors, though defenders of the practice argue it can be necessary to retain talent in turbulent times. Critics argue repricing flies in the face of holding managers accountable for stock performance.

"The pricing represents a significant giveaway to executives," wrote Amy Pessetto, an analyst with VerityData, which tracks insider holdings for investors.

A Trade Desk spokesman said repricing was "a more disciplined choice than issuing new awards" and was intended to motivate employees.

"We felt strongly that this was the best decision for employees, customers and shareholders and are confident in our path forward," the spokesman said.

Shareholders approved the move this week in a nearly 2-to-1 vote, though that was because Green's shares alone added up to about 98% of the "yes" vote. The CEO and co-founder holds just over 50% of Trade Desk's voting power, thanks largely to supervoting shares, according to a September securities filing by Trade Desk.

Absent his shares, the vote would have failed with about 95% opposed, VerityData concluded.

"In effect, Green carried a vote on repricing his own options over the clear objection of outside shareholders," Pessetto wrote. "The optics are bad and the repricing shows little confidence that the stock can recover to the original strikes on its own."

To keep the new price, executives and employees must remain employed and wait until at least April 19 to exercise the options, "which ties their outcome directly to shareholders," the Trade Desk spokesman said. The repricing also applied to options on just over 12 million shares held by more than 2,300 other company employees. In September, the company said it was laying off 15% of its workforce, which stood at 3,800 people at the end of 2025.

The slump in Trade Desk's shares has slashed as much as $2.7 billion in value from Green's stake in the company since mid-2025, leaving him holding just under $700 million in shares at Friday's share price.

The year brought some bright spots for Green, however. In September — after the board approved repricing the options and before the shareholder vote — Trade Desk's directors granted Green an additional one-time special award of stock options on seven million shares with a strike price of $14.97. The new options vest if Trade Desk's stock reaches price thresholds from $18 to $105 a share.

Since 2021, U.S. publicly traded companies have repriced options around 220 times, VerityData found, many of them small and microcap biotechnology companies with volatile shares and long strategic horizons. Around a third of the time, repricing excluded top executives.

Moderna repriced options for nonexecutive employees in late 2025, reducing the number of shares underlying the instruments. Zillow repriced options in 2022, and EchoStar did in 2024, VerityData said.

Write to Theo Francis at theo.francis@wsj.com

data.title: Elon Musk Is ‘Okay With Being Disliked’ — and He Knows Exactly Where His $985 Billion Fortune Is Going
data.description:
Elon Musk is the world’s richest person, currently worth nearly $1 trillion, a milestone he became the first to hit earlier this year. Musk is also the most followed person on social media platform X with more than 240 million followers.

Here’s what Musk wants his legacy to be and where his money should go after he passes.

Musk on Being Liked

In a new interview with author Walter Isaacson, Musk covers his thoughts on key topics like artificial intelligence and more. He also shares details about his personal life and ideals, similar to what Isaacson wrote in a biography of the billionaire several years ago.

"Sometimes I don’t like to be liked," Musk said. "I’m okay with being disliked."

Musk told Isaacson on "The Builders" podcast that wanting to be liked could be a bad quality for building a company, as things may not work out if you are doing things that diminish the success rate of the company in order to be liked.

While Musk recognizes that many people don’t like him, he highlights his large social media following and predicts that, among people who know who he is, 70% to 80% like him.

"Some people hate my guts."

Musk’s Legacy

Musk has plenty of thoughts on how AI and robots could create universal income and wealth for everyone and make money obsolete. If that happens, his current $985 billion net worth could be changed.

"The future is going to be AI and robots," Musk said.

He said currency won’t matter someday. "I don’t think money’s going to matter in the future."

If money does matter and Musk remains the richest person, he said that his descendants will have a high tax bill and may be worth less than he is.

The billionaire said most of his net worth will go towards his foundation and help preserve his legacy. Asked what he hopes his legacy will be, Musk hit on three key ideals.

The billionaire wants his wealth to "continue the goals" of making life multi-planetary, extend consciousness to the stars and improve sustainability on Earth.

data.title: FCA Proposes Crypto Crime Guidance On Wallet Checks And Blockchain Analytics
data.description:
TL;DR: The FCA is consulting on updated financial crime guidance for crypto businesses, including customer checks, blockchain analytics and the Travel Rule. Responses are due December 24, and the guide itself would not create new rules.

Crypto businesses preparing for the UK’s expanded regulatory regime have a more detailed picture of the controls the Financial Conduct Authority expects them to build.

The regulator’s October 23 consultation proposes changes to its Financial Crime Guide, covering cryptoassets alongside fraud, sanctions, data security and money laundering. The proposals apply to the FCA’s financial crime supervisory population, including cryptoasset businesses and firms overseen under the Money Laundering Regulations.

The practical focus is on how firms assess customers and transactions, and how they react when risk changes. A blockchain record can help an investigation, but a record alone does not decide whether a customer explanation is credible or a transfer needs further scrutiny.

Analytics Must Sit Inside A Working Control System

The consultation paper proposes examples of good and poor practice for enhanced due diligence, onboarding and transaction monitoring. It specifically addresses the use of blockchain analytics and further guidance on the Travel Rule, which concerns information accompanying certain transfers.

The paper also reminds firms that governance must evolve as their businesses grow. Its proposed changes include a question about whether policies and staff training distinguish obligations under proceeds-of-crime legislation from those under terrorism legislation.

For an exchange or provider of custody, the implication is that buying a screening product is only one part of the job. Someone still has to set its thresholds, review alerts and document decisions. A technically accurate warning is of limited use if it sits unreviewed while funds move elsewhere.

That matters for stablecoin transfers as much as for volatile tokens. A stable unit price does not establish the identity of a sender or the origin of funds. Transaction risk and market risk are different questions, and control systems need to reflect that distinction.

Guidance Now, A Wider Regime In 2027

The FCA says the guide contains no rules and imposes no new requirements. It is intended to help firms understand supervisory expectations and assess their own arrangements. The consultation closes on December 24, after which the regulator plans to publish feedback and the final text in a policy statement.

Separately, the FCA’s regime overview says the wider cryptoasset framework is expected to begin on October 25, 2027. Applications for authorization are already open, and the regulator published a package of final rules in June.

The distinction between those stages matters for firms planning investment in compliance. This consultation does not postpone existing anti-money-laundering duties until next year, nor does it bring the whole future regime into force immediately. It fills in the proposed guidance firms can use when translating their obligations into day-to-day decisions.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: SA Asks: How much could Tesla be worth in a merger deal?
data.description:
On Tuesday, Elon Musk revealed that Tesla and SpaceX have established committees to explore a merger combination.

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Danil Sereda, Victor Dergunov, and Carla Magliocco how much they thought Tesla could be worth in a merger deal.

Danil Sereda: There are actually many moving parts here. Usually, boards establish independent special committees to determine the price. Musk said the companies had already formed special committees, so I'd expect the merger to close within the next year or two.

We know that Tesla produces positive operating cash flow (>$18B on a TTM basis, per Seeking Alpha). It also holds ~$43.5B in liquid cash and investments, whereas SpaceX burned over $42B in CapEx on a TTM basis (mainly on its orbital infrastructure and AI-related stuff). So I agree with some analysts who say that Tesla shareholders might be willing to take >50% control of the combined entity (that's an assumption from Morningstar).

I'll take 50% here to account for SPCX's structurally higher valuation at the start because it has more growth pillars. At 50% of the combined market cap right now (~$3.5T), I'm getting to $1.75T for TSLA, which has ~3.95B diluted shares outstanding. This gives me a fair value per share of $443, which is around 20% above today's price (I'm comparing to the pre-market price of ~$368/share on Thursday, Oct. 22). Of course, the proportion might be above 50% for Tesla, and in that case, the premium will be higher.

(Danil Sereda leads the SA investing group Beyond the Wall Investing.)

Victor Dergunov: I think SpaceX would pay $420 to $500 per share at the very least for Tesla , and that is if the deal went through in the very near term. However, the high-interest environment may push the deal to mid-2027 or so. It's possible the markets may be more optimistic because of easier Fed policy by then, and I'd prefer $550 or more for my shares, as it is my portfolio's most considerable position. I also want to increase my position on any pullbacks in Tesla's stock in future weeks and months.

Carla Magliocco: In an article I wrote in May about Tesla and its vertical integration, a user asked me how the IPO of SpaceX , which took place the following month, would affect Tesla . There were plenty of doubts about it, and it was believed that Tesla investors would sell their shares and rush toward SpaceX . But none of that happened.

So, at that moment, my answer was yes, I'd love a merger because it would unite all the potential of the physical AI that Tesla was already developing. Since at least 2023, Musk has said he wanted to base his corporate ecosystem on AI. And I believe that makes sense.

In the preview of Q3 that I wrote about Tesla earlier this week, I explained that the FSD model is precisely that: a platform that builds an empire of physical AI. In the preview, I estimated 1.62M active subscribers, but I fell short: there were 1.74M, representing 67% year-over-year growth.

But now, such a merger would benefit even more the sentiment of Tesla investors, and as I own shares of Tesla and not SpaceX , this really excites me. But it's more about a mutual benefit. SpaceX just showed in its Q3 results that its Super Intelligence segment is not only growing more than expected but is also reaching higher profitability.

Meanwhile, Tesla still doesn't show strong profitability, and that's why it needs more investment to accelerate the production of Robotaxis and Optimus and reach a more advanced FSD system without supervision. At the same time, Tesla would give SpaceX what SpaceX doesn't have: monetization of its physical AI. Therefore, I believe that any news about a merger would make Tesla rise, although the final result will depend on the terms.

data.title: Silver Price Analysis as October Sell-Off Tests the Market’s Recovery Prospects
data.description:
The swift drop in silver prices in October has put the precious metal at a pivotal level, and the metal has dropped by almost 6% over the last week.

Silver Extends Its October Decline as Selling Pressure Builds

The supplied Trading Economics chart shows silver prices dropping 5.96% for the week to $53.883 per ounce.The weekly chang show-3.412. The prices were again hovering around $53.9 on October 24, and the chart was indicating a big pullback from above $57 earlier this week.

The drop further escalated since October 22, when silver breached the $56 level and headed down to $54. Source: TradingEconomics

The price closed in the mid-$50s, before stabilising a fraction of a penny higher. The chart displays a brief period of consolidation late in the week; however, this is not yet a confirmation of a longer-term reversal.

Further market commentary also highlights yield pressures, a stronger US dollar and interest-rate expectations. On October 23, FOREX.com news agency said that silver had found a long-term support base of 50-55 after a wide precious-metals sell-off.

TradingView Signals Point to a Weak Technical Structure

As of October 24, silver was trading at $53.918 on the provided TradingView chart, which had declined by 1.26% during the session. The displayed moving averages were at $61.309 and $63.618, respectively, which were still above the price. Both were on a downward trend, suggesting that prices in recent times have been subdued during the considered time periods.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) was at 31.58, which is below the average level of 38.21. The latest reading puts silver near the 30 level, which is typically seen as oversold. Source: TradingView

But this isn't a conclusive sign of recovery, especially if the prices continue in the form of lower lows. The first important area of the technical zone is the interval between $53 and $55. Any continuation of the trend below $53 would leave the market open for more losses to the $50 price level.

On the other hand, a recovery above $55 will signal an initial stabilisation. However, with more evidence of a change in trend, silver would need to reach higher levels and test resistance at $61-$64.

These levels are technical levels that you are given in this chart and NOT guaranteed future trading levels. A change in the price action may be in sight, depending on the direction of US Treasury yields, the dollar and the general sentiment on precious metals.

October and December Forecasts rely on a Market Reversal.

October and December Forecasts Depend on a Market Reversal

However, the charts are looking for caution for the rest of the month as silver is still trading below its period averages. A break above $55 would signal a short-term recovery, while a drop below $53 would increase downside risk. The 50-55 zone continues to be significant as market analysts have found it to be a wider support area.

December is a more ambiguous month. In the August forecast, J.P. Morgan had an average of $63/oz. for Q4 and $70.60/oz. for 2026. The forecast aligned with expectations of easing physical-market tightness, declining industrial demand, and interest-rate pressures. These are average which are forecasts and do not guarantee December closing prices.

On X, Rashad Hajiyev stated that silver has formed a long-term cup and handle breakout and retest. Prices may even reach $200 by 2027, he said. Source: X Via Rashad

This, of course, is an analyst's bull case and not a market consensus or actual projection. Buyers would have needed to take control and break out of the technical resistance near $60–$63 to make a move in December.

A continued lacklustre performance may instead drag silver down to around $50–$55. The evidence provided herein suggests that the next few months are a period of caution until prices recover and cross key moving averages, but the longer-term trend depends on monetary policy, industrial demand and investment flows.

data.title: New York Seeks $1.3 Billion From NovaTech Founders In Crypto Fraud Case
data.description:
TL;DR: New York’s attorney general is seeking $1.3 billion in monetary relief in the NovaTech case and has announced nearly $6 million in promoter settlements. The larger sum is a request to the court, not money recovered for investors.

New York’s effort to recover losses from the NovaTech cryptocurrency scheme has reached a new stage, with Attorney General Letitia James asking a court to impose roughly $1.3 billion in damages and disgorgement.

The October 22 announcement also disclosed nearly $6 million in settlements with four promoters. Those are separate from the much larger claim involving founders Cynthia and Eddy Petion. The announcement does not establish that either amount has already reached victims.

The case concerns investment packages sold through NovaTech and an earlier business, AWS Mining. According to the attorney general, the schemes targeted Haitian and other immigrant communities through religious networks, social media and messaging groups.

The New Filing Follows An Earlier Judgment

An affirmation filed on October 22 supports the request for monetary relief. It records that New York sued in June 2024 and that the defaulting defendants did not respond or appear. The court entered a default order and judgment on August 4, 2025.

The latest motion asks the court to determine the financial consequences. It should not be confused with a new criminal conviction, a completed recovery or a guarantee that a judgment can be collected. Those distinctions are particularly important when the sums sought are much larger than the settlements announced alongside them.

The promoter figures listed by the attorney general are $2.9 million from Martin Zizi, $2.05 million from Frantz Ciceron, $750,000 from James Corbett and $275,861 from Ricardo Roy Sr. All four face permanent bans from the securities, commodities and cryptocurrency industries.

The timing also needs care: the Zizi consent papers were filed in November 2025. This week’s announcement brings the settlement figures together; it does not mean every agreement was signed this week.

Recruitment Promises Outran The Trading Business

The original mining operation offered high returns and recruiting bonuses, according to the court affirmation. NovaTech later marketed cryptocurrency trading packages. The cryptocurrency label described how investors supplied money, but the underlying issue was what operators actually did with it.

That is a useful distinction for readers assessing similar pitches. An account balance on a website does not establish that assets exist, that trades occurred or that withdrawals can be honored. Nor does a familiar community connection answer questions about custody and control of funds.

For affected investors, the next substantive development will be the court’s decision on monetary relief and any subsequent recovery process. The announced settlements and the requested award address different defendants and different steps in that process; combining them into a headline recovery figure would overstate what has happened.

Related reading: How crypto exchanges work.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Forget Anthropic: Biotech Is Quietly Dominating the IPO Sphere — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Paul R. La Monica

The initial public offering market has been in a lull as investors continue to wait for Claude developer Anthropic to officially file a S-1 form, with a handful of companies making their public debuts in recent weeks. Just don't tell that to biotech investors.

Five biotechs have gone public this month, and several of them have soared — including Lycia Therapeutics, which gained 67% on Friday. Lycia, which is developing drugs for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases as well as food allergies, priced its offering at $18, the high end of its range, and sold $314 million in stock in its IPO Friday. Shares closed the session at $30 but at one point, Lycia stock had more than doubled, reaching a peak of $36.49.

Lycia's IPO follows the healthy debut for City Therapeutics, a biotech that is working on drugs to treat degenerative eye condition Stargardt disease and some blood clotting disorders. City, which has partnerships with Bausch + Lomb and Biogen and counts Fidelity as a notable investor, rose nearly 30% on its first day of trading on Oct. 16. The stock has pulled back a bit since then, but is still 15% above its IPO price.

Retension Pharmaceuticals, which is developing drugs to treat high blood pressure, is up 27% since it went public on Oct. 9. In a sign that demand for the IPO was strong, Retension increased the size of the stock sale to 3.8 million shares from an original plan of 3.3 million.

Two other biotechs have made their Wall Street debuts this month, but haven't fared as well. TRex Bio, which is also working on autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, has dropped about 1% since its Oct. 8 IPO. Iambic Therapeutics, despite a 18% gain on its first day of trading on Oct. 15, is now down more than 10% from its IPO price.

Iambic, which is using AI to develop drugs to treat various forms of cancer, is backed by Cathie Wood's ARK Investment Management, Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office and Nvidia.

None of these five companies are profitable. as all are early-stage biotechs. But the fact that they have been able to make it through the IPO window at a time when other companies, such as smart ring maker Oura and Solidigm, the flash memory unit of South Korean AI chip company SK Hynix, have shelved their planned listings, is a promising sign that investors still have an appetite for some start-ups.

"Healthcare remains a bright spot," wrote Bill Smith, CEO and founder of IPO research and investing firm Renaissance Capital in a recent report. To that end, several other biotechs, including Aspen Neuroscience and Bambusa Therapeutics, filed for IPOs this month.

Still, the broader IPO market may remain in hibernation for at least another month. Smith said money companies are preferring to stay on the sideline "as most issuers wait to get past the current volatility, the midterms, and the Anthropic IPO."

A draft of Anthropic's IPO filing shows the company lost more than $80 billion in the first half of 2026, The Wall Street Journal reported. Even though more than $70 billion of that is said to be due to accounting charges, some investors may be reluctant to pay a premium for the company.

Anthropic did not immediately respond to Barron's request for comment.

The weak performance of other recent IPOs, like those of sandwich chain Jersey Mike's Subs and homeowners insurer Orion180, doesn't help, either. But for now, it looks like biotech investors are ignoring the IPO doldrums.

Write to Paul R. La Monica at paul.lamonica@barrons.com

data.title: SEC Puts Tokenization On Its 2027 Examination Agenda
data.description:
TL;DR: The SEC has named tokenization among its fiscal 2027 examination priorities, bringing the systems behind blockchain securities into closer supervisory focus. The staff document sets inspection priorities and creates no new legal obligations.

The SEC’s tokenization agenda now includes a practical question for financial firms: can the infrastructure work reliably when something goes wrong?

In its October 23 announcement, the US regulator placed tokenization among the market developments its examiners will scrutinize during fiscal 2027. The wider program also covers investment advice, complex products, private credit and cybersecurity across more than 34,000 registrants.

For companies building services around tokenized assets, that brings the discussion down from the promise of faster trading to the controls supporting it. A share recorded on a blockchain still needs dependable ownership records, functioning markets and an orderly response to disruption.

Clearing And Trading Systems Enter The Frame

The 20-page examination document explicitly includes tokenization among high-risk areas for clearing-agency reviews. In its discussion of Regulation Systems Compliance and Integrity, it lists tokenized securities alongside extended trading hours, advanced AI and quantum computing. Cloud providers and other technology suppliers also feature in those reviews.

That combination matters. Extending trading hours can leave less time for maintenance, while connecting a token to conventional securities records adds another place where systems must agree. The relevant test is whether the complete service remains dependable, including the handoffs between systems.

The document separately emphasizes cybersecurity governance, access controls, incident response and risks from shared technology. It also states that the priorities are staff views, carry no legal force and do not amend existing law. An examination focus should therefore be read as a signal about supervision, rather than a new tokenization license or prohibition.

A Permission To Experiment Still Comes With Conditions

The context is the SEC’s September innovation exemption for certain tokenized stock venues. That temporary framework requires equivalent shareholder rights, issuer notification and an opportunity to object when an unaffiliated party tokenizes shares. It also imposes trading limits and requirements for public, auditable smart contracts.

Those conditions illustrate why market access and operational supervision move together. A permitted venue can still have weak controls; a technically impressive platform can still mishandle an investor’s rights. The new priorities put attention on that gap.

For investors, the useful distinction is between the token and the service built around it. Questions about who holds the underlying security, how transactions reconcile and what happens during an outage remain relevant alongside the blockchain’s design. Custody and market infrastructure do not become incidental simply because a trade uses a token.

The SEC says its priorities are non-exhaustive and may change during the year. Tokenization’s place in the published agenda nevertheless gives firms a clear reason to expect scrutiny of how their systems operate, as well as what their products promise.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
